templates.name: Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard
templates.description: NN-4554: detects sustained metadata-lock queues and long-running Aurora queries without collecting SQL text or customer data.

items.name: Aurora guard: session counters (JSON)
items.params: SELECT COUNT(*) AS visible_session_count, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN STATE LIKE '%metadata lock%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS metadata_wait_count, COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN STATE LIKE '%metadata lock%' THEN COALESCE(TIME, 0) ELSE 0 END), 0) AS metadata_wait_max_seconds, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN COMMAND <> 'Sleep' AND COALESCE(TIME, 0) >= {$NVOIP.DB.LONG_QUERY.WARN} AND USER NOT IN ('system user', 'event_scheduler') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS long_query_count, COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN COMMAND <> 'Sleep' AND USER NOT IN ('system user', 'event_scheduler') THEN COALESCE(TIME, 0) ELSE 0 END), 0) AS longest_query_seconds FROM information_schema.PROCESSLIST WHERE ID <> CONNECTION_ID()

triggers.name: Aurora guard has no fresh sample for 2 minutes
triggers.description: The NN-4554 detector is not producing samples. Validate the ODBC DSN, database connectivity and the Zabbix database poller before treating database health as known.

triggers.name: Aurora guard cannot see other sessions
triggers.description: The ODBC account can only see its own connection. Grant the global PROCESS privilege to the dedicated read-only monitoring account; do not broaden table data access.

triggers.expression: min(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.metadata_wait.count,1m)>={$NVOIP.DB.MDL.WAIT.COUNT.WARN} and min(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.metadata_wait.max_seconds,1m)>={$NVOIP.DB.MDL.WAIT.AGE.WARN} and max(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.metadata_wait.count,1m)<{$NVOIP.DB.MDL.WAIT.COUNT.HIGH} and max(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.metadata_wait.max_seconds,1m)<{$NVOIP.DB.MDL.WAIT.AGE.HIGH}
triggers.name: Aurora has a sustained metadata-lock queue
triggers.description: At least three sessions have waited on a metadata lock for at least 30 seconds. Stop initiating maintenance DDL, identify the queued DDL and blocker, and follow the NN-4554 runbook. Do not kill application sessions automatically.

triggers.expression: min(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.metadata_wait.count,1m)>={$NVOIP.DB.MDL.WAIT.COUNT.HIGH} or min(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.metadata_wait.max_seconds,1m)>={$NVOIP.DB.MDL.WAIT.AGE.HIGH}
triggers.name: Aurora metadata-lock queue is threatening availability
triggers.description: The metadata-lock queue crossed the NN-4554 high threshold. Treat this as an availability incident. Identify the queued maintenance DDL first; do not automatically kill application sessions or transactions.

items.name: Aurora guard: oldest metadata lock wait

triggers.expression: min(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.long_query.count,2m)>=1 and max(/Template Nvoip Aurora Lock Guard/nvoip.db.longest_query.seconds,2m)<{$NVOIP.DB.LONG_QUERY.HIGH}
triggers.name: Aurora has a query running longer than {$NVOIP.DB.LONG_QUERY.WARN} seconds
triggers.description: A non-sleeping foreground query remained over the warning threshold for two minutes. Inspect ownership and impact before taking action; there is no automatic KILL.

triggers.name: Aurora has a query running longer than {$NVOIP.DB.LONG_QUERY.HIGH} seconds
triggers.description: A non-sleeping foreground query crossed the high threshold. Inspect the query owner, transaction and blockers. Never kill a production query solely from this trigger.
